value.definition: memory a program could take without anything being swapped

invariants.statement: Memory that is free is a part of memory that is available.
Cached memory the kernel would give up counts as available.
A host with little free memory and much available has nothing wrong with it.
Whether a host can admit more work is asked in available memory.

value.definition: memory holding what was read from disk, kept until something else wants it

invariants.statement: Cached memory reads as used and is given up on demand.
Cached memory is given up rather than swapped when a program asks.
A host whose memory reads as nearly all used is often nearly all cache.
Memory a process holds is never given up this way.

value.definition: a shared page divided among the processes holding that page

invariants.statement: Proportional memory over every process on a host adds to what that host holds.
The proportional memory of a process holding nothing shared is its resident memory.
A process's proportional memory rises when a process sharing with it ends.

value.definition: memory a process holds in RAM at the moment it is read

invariants.statement: Two processes sharing a page are each resident in the whole page.
Adding the resident memory of two processes counts a page they share twice.
Memory a process has swapped out is resident nowhere.
What one process is holding is asked in resident memory.

value.definition: memory more than one process holds at once

invariants.statement: A page more than one process holds is held once by the host.
Shared memory is why the processes of a host add to more than that host has.
A library every process loads is shared rather than held by each.
Ending one process holding a shared page frees none of that page.

value.definition: disk a host holds a process's memory in while that process is not reaching it

invariants.statement: Swapped memory is counted against the process holding it.
Reaching swapped memory costs thousands of times what reaching RAM costs.
A host is unusable from swapping long before that host's swap is gone.
Swap left is no sign a host has memory to spare.
Swap of more than one kind is taken in the order the priorities state.
A host with no swap at all is a host whose swap is drained.

value.definition: memory a process has asked for rather than memory that process holds

invariants.statement: Memory a process asked for and never reached costs that process no RAM.
A process's virtual memory bounds nothing about what that process holds.
A runtime reserving its whole heap at once is virtual until reached.
The address space limit an rlimit states is read in virtual memory.
